newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Diesel sets new operating structure.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Diesel sets new operating structure.

text.p: Detroit Diesel Corp, which posted a slight increase in fourth quarter net income to $4.6 million, said Wednesday it is setting up a new operating structure to improve customer responsiveness and profits.

The new operating structure will have nine businesses based on eight engine families and Detroit Diesel Capital Corp, the company's wholesale financing arm. Each product line will be managed by a general manager who has responsibility for performance and profitability for the unit.
The maker of heavy-duty engines earned $0.19 a share in the fourth quarter of 1996. A year ago, the company earned $4.5 million or $0.18.

Detroit Diesel said its results reflect the competitive environment for heavy-duty engines. Total 1996 shipments fell six percent to 156,710, while heavy-duty truck engine shipments were down 22 percent.

For the quarter, on-highway truck revenues were down 12 percent to $182 million; construction and industrial revenues grew five percent to $100 million; automotive revenues were up 23 percent to $65 million; and coach and bus revenues rose 17 percent to $61 million.
